title: Where Unkindness Learns Its Name

features.name: the country learning its outline
features.desc-on-touch: You trace the line where this land stops and names itself. There is no cruelty here—only clarity. The earth knows what it is.

features.name: the honest field
features.desc-on-touch: This paddock asks nothing of you. It does not comfort. It stands named and austere and tells you exactly what it is and nothing more.

features.name: the stone that refused kindness and found its shape
features.desc-on-touch: Stone here is sharp-edged, unsmoothed. It learned that it did not need kindness to have form. The lack of gentleness made it more itself.

features.name: the arch where the threshold names itself backwards
features.desc-on-touch: You pass under and the country you came from falls away. Here it calls itself by its true name—not by what it lacks, but by what it is.

features.name: the eucalyptus that learned to stand alone
features.desc-on-touch: A tree knows it does not need shade-kindness or comfort-water. It simply grows where it grows. The unkind country taught it this.

reverie.title: REVERIE — learning to call the place by its true name
narr: you walked across the open land that wanted nothing from you.
she said: this is easier than kindness. the ground doesn't ask
you to soften. you don't have to return the comfort. you could
both just walk and let the place call itself what it was. the
light was very clear. you asked what the name was. she smiled:
the same as it always was. we just stopped pretending it was kind.

inscription: the country that does not comfort learns to call itself by its true name; unkindness is only the absence of pretending to be kind
